intro.TrustedMarkup:
Waiting for the host: sleep, the host's timer, and the run queue.

A function that reaches a wait waits itself, and each call of it is marked await (language.md, Waiting).

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits while the host runs other tasks, until ms milliseconds after the deadline of the wake this task runs in, or after the start of the program or of the request: the time the task computes before it counts against it.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Both<A, B> = { first: A, second: B }

prose.TrustedMarkup: The results of the two tasks of a both, in argument order.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Race<A, B> = enum { First(A), Second(B) }

prose.TrustedMarkup: The task of a race that returned first, and its result.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Joined<T> = enum { Done(T), Cancelled(Task<T>) }

prose.TrustedMarkup: What joinOr answers: the task's result, or its handle when the caller was cancelled while it waited.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn join<T>(t: consume Task<T>) -> T

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits for t to end and returns its result. If t is cancelled, the caller is cancelled where it waits.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn joinOr<T>(t: consume Task<T>) -> Joined<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits for t as join does, but a cancellation of the caller while it waits here answers Cancelled(t), and the caller runs on: it decides to cancel, keep or hand on t, and returns. Any other wait the caller reaches after that ends it there. If t is cancelled, the caller is cancelled where it waits.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn cancel<T>(t: consume Task<T>)

prose.TrustedMarkup: Ends t where it waits, releasing what it holds, or releases its result when it returned. Does not wait.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn both<A, B>(first: consume Task<A>, second: consume Task<B>) -> Both<A, B>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits for both tasks: their results, in argument order. If one is cancelled, both cancels the other and is cancelled. If the caller is cancelled while it waits here, both cancels both tasks.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn race<A, B>(first: consume Task<A>, second: consume Task<B>) -> Race<A, B>

prose.TrustedMarkup: The first task to return, in argument order once both started, and its result: await race(fork f(a), fork sleep(500)). The other is cancelled where it waits, or released if it returned. If the first to end was cancelled, race is cancelled. If the caller is cancelled while it waits here, race cancels both tasks.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn timeout<T>(ms: Int64, t: consume Task<T>) -> Option<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Some of t's result if it returns within ms milliseconds, else None, and t is cancelled where it waits.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn joinAll<T>(ts: consume Array<Task<T>>) -> Array<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits for every task: the results, in index order. If one is cancelled, or the caller is cancelled while it waits here, joinAll cancels the rest and is cancelled.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Group<T> = { tasks: Array<Task<T>>, ids: Array<Int64>, limit: Int64 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: Tasks of one result type, at most limit of them running at once, joined or cancelled together; ids holds their run queue ids in the same order.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn group<T>(limit: Int64 where value >= 1) -> Group<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup: An empty group whose tasks run at most limit at once. A limit below 1 traps at the call, because room would wait forever.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn room<T>(g: modify Group<T>)

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits until fewer than the limit of g's tasks run: call it before each fork the group will hold. If one was cancelled, or the caller is cancelled while it waits here, room cancels the group's tasks and is cancelled.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn add<T>(g: modify Group<T>, t: consume Task<T>)
fn joinGroup<T>(g: consume Group<T>) -> Array<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Waits for every task of g: the results, in the order they were added.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn cancelGroup<T>(g: consume Group<T>)

prose.TrustedMarkup: Cancels every task of g where it waits.
